title: Propagation Quality Auditor and Sampled Context Reconstructor
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Background: We frequently see partial or broken trace chains from edge SDKs and async workers where propagation headers are dropped or rewritten (mobile SDKs, queued workers, and legacy proxies). This hurts root cause analysis and inflates P95 latency investigation time. Goal: build a lightweight, sampling-aware Propagation Quality Auditor (PQA) that scores incoming requests on propagation fidelity and a Sampled Context Reconstructor (SCR) that attempts non-invasive reconstruction of lost trace context for sampled traces. The auditor will emit telemetry about propagation gaps and reconstruction attempts; the reconstructor will populate an advisory context envelope that downstream services can use for best-effort stitching without breaking existing trace semantics.

Scope and constraints: Keep changes minimal in SDKs (JS, Python, Go) — primarily add a nonblocking middleware hook and a small client-side scorer library. Reconstruction logic must avoid leaking PII and should only act on traces that are sampled. The solution must not increase request latency above our 99th percentile SLOs (target < 0.5ms added on hot paths) and should be toggleable via SDK config and Central Config flags.

High-level acceptance criteria: (1) PQA emits a per-request propagation_score (0-100) with reasons for deduction; (2) SCR produces an advisory context when reconstruction succeeds, tagged as "best_effort_reconstructed"; (3) Instrumentation is added to Console dashboards showing reconstructed vs original trace counts, reconstruction success rate, and any correlation with downstream error rates; (4) Rollout via feature flag to 10% of traffic with safe rollback.

Design notes and heuristics: The PQA will look at header patterns (x-trace-id, swTrace, b3, traceparent) and attribute heuristics like header TTL, mismatch between incoming sampling hint and carrier sampling bit, and aberrant path-length deltas. We will score header chain integrity and add synthetic hints such as parent_id_entropy. SCR will use three staged heuristics: 1) deterministic stitching by canonical id normalization (when only casing, separator differences exist), 2) sampled-session correlation using ephemeral session tokens (when present), 3) probabilistic reconstruction using temporal-parent scoring and bounded fan-in (last resort; only for sampled traces and with risk window). All reconstruction outputs must include metadata about confidence and origin so downstream systems can ignore low-confidence stitches during precision-sensitive joins.

Implementation plan: phase 1 (week 1) — spec and SDK hook prototypes (JS and Go); phase 2 (week 2) — central collector schema + Console visualizations; phase 3 (week 3) — staged rollout + A/B telemetry; phase 4 (post-rollout) — iterate on heuristics and add more SDK languages. We will gate heavy heuristics behind telemetry budget and provide a kill-switch.

Instrumentation and privacy: emitted telemetry will be limited to hashed identifiers and counters; we will not emit full request payloads. Work will include a security review to confirm no PII leakage.
acceptance_criteria: Propagation Quality Auditor emits propagation_score and deduction_reasons for 100% of flagged requests
Sampled Context Reconstructor returns advisory context with confidence metadata for reconstructed traces when sampling bit is set
Console dashboard shows reconstruction_success_rate, propagation_score histogram, and top deduction reasons
Feature-flagged rollout to 10% traffic with automated rollback on error rate regression > 0.5% relative increase
plan: Lightweight SDK hook implemented for JS and Go with nonblocking scoring API
Collector schema change (observability.events.propagation_audit) and migration plan
Dashboard prototype in Console and a shortlink to prototype dashboard: /console/dashboards/propagation-auditor
Staged rollout: QA -> internal prod (10%) -> 50% -> 100% with telemetry checks
risks: False positives from probabilistic reconstruction could create noisy joins in debug flows
Telemetry volume increase if auditing is enabled wide; must enforce sampling and aggregation
SDK adoption lag across languages could lead to inconsistent telemetry coverage
Edge proxies might rewrite headers in ways our heuristics do not account for
